Plot Stacked Landings or Biomass by Group

plot_landings_stacked.Rd

Visualizes fisheries landings or biomass trends over time using a stacked area plot. Supports bilingual labeling (via an internal dictionary and rosettafish), custom color palettes, and adjustable text scaling. Automatically detects the legend title (Group vs Guild) and stacking order based on the content of the data.

Usage

plot_landings_stacked(
  data,
  year_col = year,
  group_col = grp,
  value_col = landings,
  lang = "en",
  year_range = NULL,
  group_order = NULL,
  show_title = FALSE,
  col_palette = NULL,
  base_size = 14,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  x_breaks = NULL,
  y_breaks = ggplot2::waiver(),
  custom_theme = ggplot2::theme_bw()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing landings or biomass.

year_col

Unquoted name of the year column. Defaults to year.

group_col

Unquoted name of the grouping column (e.g., species group). Defaults to grp.

value_col

Unquoted name of the landings or biomass value column. Defaults to landings.

lang

Language for labels: "en" (default) or "fr".

year_range

Numeric vector c(start, end) to filter the timeline.

group_order

Character vector defining the visual order from top to bottom. If NULL, the function auto-detects based on species names in the data.

show_title

Logical. Defaults to FALSE.

col_palette

Optional named character vector of colors.

base_size

Numeric. Base font size for the plot. Defaults to 14.

xlab, ylab

Optional strings to override default axis labels.

legend_title

Optional string to override the automatic legend title detection.

x_breaks

Optional numeric vector for x-axis tick marks (e.g. seq(1990, 2025, 5)).

y_breaks

Optional numeric vector for y-axis tick marks. Defaults to ggplot2::waiver() (automatic).

custom_theme

A ggplot2 theme. Defaults to theme_bw().

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load your data
landings_data <- read.csv("landings_by_group.csv")

# 1. Basic plot with default order (Top: Pelagics -> Middle: Crustaceans -> Bottom: Groundfish)
plot_landings_stacked(landings_data)

# 2. French version, custom year range, and larger text scaling
plot_landings_stacked(landings_data,
                       lang = "fr",
                       year_range = c(1990, 2023),
                       base_size = 16)

# 3. Custom stack order: Pelagics on top, Crustaceans on bottom
plot_landings_stacked(landings_data,
                       group_order = c("pelagics", "groundfish", "crustaceans"))

# 4. Custom colour palette with rosettafish fallback
my_pal <- c("Crustaceans" = "#8b0000",
             "Groundfish"  = "#4682b4",
             "Pelagics"    = "#2e8b57")

plot_landings_stacked(landings_data, col_palette = my_pal)
} # }
